exposure: Risk factors for ectopic pregnancy (pelvic inflammatory disease, previous surgery, abortions)
Clinical presentation (amenorrhea, abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, forniceal fullness, tenderness)
cohort: The study included 100 diagnosed cases of ectopic pregnancy attending a tertiary care hospital in West Bengal, India.
finding: A significant majority (86%) of ectopic pregnancy cases presented with ruptured ectopic pregnancies, necessitating emergency surgery in most patients (94%), predominantly salpingectomy (85%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023.
gest_age: A majority (62%) of patients presented between 6 and 8 weeks of amenorrhea.
